# Transport basic-quiver ISA — v0.16

Let `A = End^*(Q6)_Q`.  In the split carrier bases of v0.15 every element is uniquely

\[
T_+=\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\0&I_2\otimes S\end{pmatrix},\qquad
T_-=\begin{pmatrix}A&B\\0&I_3\otimes S\end{pmatrix},
\]

with `a in Q`, `A in M15(Q)`, `S in M5(Q)`, two plus-arrow blocks `u_1,u_2 in M_{1x5}(Q)`, and three minus-arrow blocks `v_1,v_2,v_3 in M_{15x5}(Q)`.  This is the native amplified five-arrow ISA.

## Theorem 1 — relation-free native multiplication

For elements `x=(a,A,S,u_i,v_j)` and `y=(a',A',S',u_i',v_j')`,

\[
xy=(aa',AA',SS',\;a u_i'+u_iS',\;Av_j'+v_jS').
\]

There are no arrow-arrow terms because the Jacobson radical is square-zero.  Hence the old 25+412 two-generator rewrite rules are no longer part of execution semantics; they remain only a reproduction certificate for the historical two-generator encoding.

The package freezes an explicit tensor-normalizing bridge from the stored v0.15 complements and an 8-dimensional corner basis whose multiplication table is exactly the three-vertex/five-arrow radical-square-zero path algebra.

## Theorem 2 — Morita descent of the degree-46 unit divisor

The old transport unit polynomial is

\[
\Delta=\det(S)\det(T_+)\det(T_-).
\]

In native coordinates,

\[
\det(T_+)=a\det(S)^2,\qquad
\det(T_-)=\det(A)\det(S)^3,
\]

so

\[
\boxed{\Delta=a\det(A)\det(S)^6.}
\]

Thus the radical arrows do not participate in invertibility.  A native element is a unit iff

\[
a\ne0,\qquad A\in GL_{15},\qquad S\in GL_5.
\]

On the Morita basic algebra the reduced support of the divisor is simply

\[
\boxed{\delta_{\rm basic}=\alpha\beta\gamma,}
\]

the product of the three vertex coordinates.  On central scalar matrices the original determinant multiplicities are `(1,15,30)`.

The inverse is also native:

\[
u_i^{\,-1}=-a^{-1}u_iS^{-1},\qquad
v_j^{\,-1}=-A^{-1}v_jS^{-1}.
\]

## Theorem 3 — hard-negative certificates are an external Morita boundary

The characteristic-zero hard-negative pairs `Q2/Q35` and `Q159/Q160` do not belong to the positive species-3 additive component generated by `Q6`.  Therefore their canonical-factor/projective determinant semi-invariants are not regular functions on the 8-dimensional basic algebra `eAe` and do not canonically "descend" to five scalar arrow coordinates.

The correct Forge architecture is two-stage:

1. **ambient object gate:** canonical factors and projective semi-invariants decide component admission and separate hard negatives;
2. **internal transport compiler:** after admission to the positive species-3 component, compile all morphisms using the three vertex payloads and five arrow payloads, with the vertex unit test above.

This is not a loss of information under Morita equivalence.  Morita equivalence is applied to the positive component category itself; the hard-negative objects lie outside that category and are boundary data for deciding whether the component model applies.

## Evidence boundary

The characteristic-zero formulas follow from the exact v0.15 block theorem.  The package-local implementation is independently checked modulo the frozen good prime `1,000,003`: random 486-coordinate elements round-trip through the native bridge, random products agree with the stored transport multiplication, random units invert exactly, and the explicit 8-element corner basis satisfies the basic path-algebra multiplication table.  The projective hard-negative signatures are copied from the already-certified species-1/2 good-reduction ledgers; they are not used as native quiver inputs.
